items.title: MOSS-Audio request-controlled processor cache permits remote memory exhaustion
Unbounded Prometheus label cardinality from attacker-controlled HTTP method tokens in the vLLM Rust frontend metrics middleware (unauthenticated denial of service)
Denial of service: a negative token id in `/v1/embeddings` or `/pooling` input kills the vLLM engine via a CUDA device-side assertion
Qwen2-VL / Qwen3-VL video samplers bound on request-controlled max_frames, which the num_frames ceiling does not reach
GLMGA video sampling permits request-driven CPU and memory exhaustion
vLLM DoS via unbounded `cache_salt` length: multi-hundred-MB salt stalls the single EngineCore scheduler thread (CPU exhaustion)
Forged multimodal UUID + P0/P1 processor-cache eviction drift: unauthenticated remote crash of the whole vLLM engine
V1 InputBatch.condense leaves a stale allowed_token_ids mask on recycled batch rows
Request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision allows remote code execution
An oversized min_tokens in one request hangs the vLLM engine while /health stays green

event.title: MOSS-Audio request-controlled processor cache permits remote memory exhaustion

claims.display_value:
### Summary

  When vLLM serves a MOSS-Audio model, a client that can access the /tokenize endpoint can provide request-controlled
  mm_processor_kwargs.

  MOSS-Audio uses these values to construct MossAudioProcessor instances and stores every distinct instance in an
  unbounded private dictionary. Each processor contains a WhisperFeatureExtractor with an allocated mel-filter array.

  An attacker can therefore:

  1. Repeatedly submit distinct processor configurations to cause persistent linear memory growth.
  2. Supply oversized mel_config values to amplify the allocation made by a single request.

  This can exhaust host memory and terminate or severely degrade the API process. /tokenize is intentionally outside
  vLLM’s API-key-protected route prefixes, so --api-key alone does not restrict access to this endpoint.

  ### Details

  TokenizeChatRequest accepts arbitrary mm_processor_kwargs
  (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bf7eee9d7b2788bafe69f0c21fde6af22a2d3319/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/protocol.py#L107-L110).

  The request reaches multimodal processing through:

  1. ServingTokenization.create_tokenize()

     (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bf7eee9d7b2788bafe69f0c21fde6af22a2d3319/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/serving.py#L84-L92)

  2. OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat()

     (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bf7eee9d7b2788bafe69f0c21fde6af22a2d3319/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L675-L704)

  3. BaseRenderer._process_multimodal()

     (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bf7eee9d7b2788bafe69f0c21fde6af22a2d3319/vllm/renderers/base.py#L846-L880)

  4. MossAudioMultiModalProcessor._apply_hf_processor_main()

     (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bf7eee9d7b2788bafe69f0c21fde6af22a2d3319/vllm/model_executor/models/moss_audio.py#L1358-L1400)

  Although /tokenize sets skip_mm_cache=True, this only selects the read-only multimodal processor. Its

claims.display_value: Portkey AI Gateway 1.14.0 through 1.15.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach loopback and Docker host services because isValidCustomHost trusts localhost-style hosts when TRUSTED_CUSTOM_HOSTS is unset. Attackers can send /v1 requests with a crafted x-portkey-custom-host header, such as via the ollama provider, to make the gateway call internal services and return their responses.
